descricao_original: These images show the structure of the renal calyx (left) in a uni-pyramidal kidney, and the mucosa of the calyx at higher magnification (right). A calyx surrounds each pyramid, and its mucosa is reflected onto the conical surface of the pyramid. 100x, 800x.
creditos_identificados: Image source: This image was taken from a slide in the Drexel University slide collection.

marcadores.explicacao_original: The renal pyramid is a conical-shaped structure, but only its apex, the papilla (outlined), is visible in this image. The papilla of the pyramid receives the terminal ends of the papillary ducts of Bellini. The number of renal pyramids varies between species: humans have 8-10 pyramids. This image shows an example of a uni-pyramidal kidney.

marcadores.explicacao_original: The calyx, a chalice-like covering over the papilla, receives urine from the papillary ducts of Bellini. The transitional epithelium of the calyx (arrows) is reflected onto the surface of the papilla to enclose the lumen of the calyx (filled in blue).
